subject: Clarifying 'Service Provider' scope under CCPA for subprocessor onboarding
messages:
From: Sarah Lynch <sarah.lynch@acmeretail.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acmeretail.com
Date: 2026-07-10T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Service provider definition + subprocessor notice (CCPA/CPRA)

Hi Hannah / Rishi,

Thanks for sending the DPA draft. Our privacy team has a couple of specific asks related to US state privacy (CCPA/CPRA) that we need clarified before we can move forward:

1) Definition of "Service Provider" — the draft uses a broad definition that could capture downstream analytics and infrastructure partners. Under CPRA, we need confirmation that Redwood will treat those downstream vendors as "Service Providers" only when acting on Acme Retail's instructions and will not use our data for other commercial purposes.

2) Subprocessor onboarding / notice — our procurement requires at least 30 days' notice prior to onboarding any new subprocessor that will process personal data of CA residents, with the ability to object for regulatory or contractual reasons.

3) Cross-border transfer mechanism — please confirm what mechanism Redwood will rely on for transfers of personal data within the US and to remote cloud regions, and if those flows will be reflected in the subprocessor list.

We attached a redline of a couple of clauses and our required notice language (see attached). Can you confirm whether Redwood can sign with these changes or propose alternative wording?

Thanks,
Sarah
Legal Counsel, Acme Retail

Attachments: acme_dpa_redlines.docx

From: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lynch <sarah.lynch@acmeretail.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-10T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Service provider definition + subprocessor notice (CCPA/CPRA)

Hi Sarah — really helpful notes, thanks. High-level answers before we dig into specific redlines:

- Service Provider scope: Redwood's standard position is that downstream vendors used to provide the service (e.g., telemetry vendors, hosted metrics, CDN) are subprocessors and will only be authorized to process data in accordance with our instructions under the DPA. Redwood does not use customer personal data for our own commercial purposes; that restriction is in section 3 of the attached DPA.

- Subprocessor notice: We can commit to a 30-day published notice period for new subprocessors and maintain a current list (updated monthly). For cases where there is a regulatory constraint or a material change, we are open to providing earlier notice or additional detail.

- Transfers: For US-region deployments we rely on our US cloud providers and internal controls; transfers to other regions are governed by the transfer section in the DPA and will be documented on the subprocessor list.

I attached our v3 DPA and the current subprocessor list for review. Rishi / Priyom, can you weigh in on whether the 30-day notice + published list is sufficient for Acme's procurement ask, and whether we need a carveout around emergency security subprocessors?

Best,
Hannah
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf, subprocessor_list_202607.pdf

From: legal@acmeretail.com <legal@acmeretail.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: Sarah Lynch <sarah.lynch@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2026-07-11T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Service provider definition + subprocessor notice (CCPA/CPRA)

Hannah,

Thanks for the quick responses and the attachments. A couple of follow-ups from our side after an internal review:

- The language in section 3 is promising, but we need explicit anti-use language in the definition of "Service Provider" (i.e., no secondary use of personal data, no targeted advertising, and no sale as defined by state law).

- The 30-day published notice is acceptable in principle, but procurement requires an objection right that allows us to pause onboarding where a new subprocessor would create a regulatory or contractual conflict. We don't expect to use it often; typically we'd request additional controls or a short remediation plan.

- Please confirm whether Redwood will allow us to receive audit reports for subprocessors upon request (SOC 2 type II or equivalent) and whether Redwood will include subprocessors that only process metadata/pseudonymized telemetry in the published list.

If you can incorporate explicit anti-use language and an objection mechanism limited to regulatory/conflict reasons, we can move toward signature.

Regards,
Acme Retail Legal

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: Sarah Lynch <sarah.lynch@acmeretail.com>, legal@acmeretail.com
Date: 2026-07-12T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Service provider definition + subprocessor notice (CCPA/CPRA)

On Mon, Jul 12, 2026 at 01:05 PM PDT, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com wrote:
> Hi team — quick internal note on the operational side:
>
> - Audit access: we can provide SOC 2 summary reports and redacted attestations for subprocessors. Where customers require direct access, we typically accept an obligation to pursue reasonable efforts to obtain and share such reports, subject to NDAs and third-party restrictions.
> - Subprocessor list: we will include any entity that processes user-identifiable personal data. Services that only process aggregated, pseudonymized telemetry will be listed separately ("telemetry-only partners") to reduce noise.
> - Objection workflow: propose the following narrow flow: Acme provides written objection within 30 days of notice specifying regulatory/contractual basis; Redwood will either (a) delay onboarding and provide mitigation, (b) remove the subprocessor for Acme-specific deployments where feasible, or (c) terminate the engagement with 60 days' notice if an acceptable mitigation cannot be found.
>
> Priyom — does this align with ops and security?
>
> Rishi

Thanks,
Rishi 
Head of Infrastructure & Ops, Redwood Inference

From: priyom.das@redwood.com <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: Sarah Lynch <sarah.lynch@acmeretail.com>, legal@acmeretail.com
Date: 2026-07-14T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Service provider definition + subprocessor notice (CCPA/CPRA)

Sarah / Acme team —

Thanks for the constructive feedback. We can accept the following as a compromise to cover your procurement and CPRA concerns:

1) Definition: Insert explicit anti-use language into the DPA definition of Service Provider: "Redwood and its subprocessors will not use, sell, or otherwise disclose Customer personal data for purposes unrelated to providing the contracted services, including for targeted advertising or monetization."

2) Notice & objection process: Redwood will publish a monthly subprocessor list and provide 30 days' advance notice for onboarding any subprocessor that processes personal data of US residents. Acme may object in writing within 30 days on regulatory or contractual grounds; Redwood will follow the proposed mitigation flow (delay + remediation / removal for Acme-specific deployments / termination with 60 days' notice).

3) Audit reports: Redwood will provide SOC 2 summary reports and will use reasonable efforts to obtain and share subprocessor SOC reports; direct customer audit rights will be considered case-by-case with appropriate NDAs and third-party consents.

If this aligns with your procurement requirements we will prepare a short addendum (US State Privacy Addendum) to attach to the DPA with the three items above and the updated subprocessor list.

I'll circulate the addendum draft tomorrow.

Thanks,
Priyom
Director, Security & Product Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachments: (none)
